meta.title: WordPress Website Fixes — speed, bugs, stability
meta.description: I fix WordPress websites that lose leads because they are slow, buggy, or unstable. 10+ years of experience, 500+ projects, fast diagnosis, and a clear action plan.

hero.title: I fix WordPress websites that lose leads because they are slow, buggy, or unstable
hero.subtitle: I quickly find the technical root cause, fix it carefully without unnecessary plugins, and show the result in a clear “before / after” summary.

benefits.title: What you get
benefits.body: A clear plan, step-by-step execution, and a summary of “before / after”. If the task can’t be solved with a “quick fix”, I’ll tell you upfront.

when.title: When it makes sense to reach out

items.mobile: The website loads slowly on mobile
items.plugins: There are many plugins, but it is unclear what slows the site down
items.pagespeed: PageSpeed shows issues, but there is no clear action plan
items.legacy: Previous changes made the website harder to maintain

performance.title: Your website loads slowly and loses potential clients
performance.body: I speed up WordPress without breaking layouts, forms, checkout, or critical functionality: LCP/CLS/INP, CSS, JS, fonts, images, caching, and server setup.

fixes.title: Bugs block leads, sales, or normal website operation
fixes.body: I fix issues with themes, plugins, forms, multilingual setups, WooCommerce, and integrations. First I find the root cause, then I fix it without side effects.

maintenance.title: The website should stay stable instead of creating emergencies
maintenance.body: I handle updates, backups, security, monitoring, and regular improvements so the website stays reliable and does not interrupt business processes.

step1.title: 1) Diagnosis
step1.body: I review symptoms, logs, Lighthouse/PSI, plugins, theme, and critical requests. Then I compile a short list of root causes.

step2.title: 2) Plan & estimate
step2.body: I prioritize what brings the biggest impact with the lowest risk. We agree on scope, timing, and reporting format.

step3.title: 3) Implementation
step3.body: Step-by-step with checkpoints. If needed — staging/backup, targeted changes, minimal “magic”.

step4.title: 4) Verification & summary
step4.body: Re-testing, “before/after” measurements, and a list of what was done. I also suggest next steps if you want more gains.

proof.title: Proof: reviews and portfolio
proof.note: You can quickly assess my level from reviews and examples. If needed, I’ll send relevant cases for your specific task.

oneTime.title: One-off task
oneTime.body: For a specific fix/improvement/small audit. Best when you need something done “right now” and the scope is clear.

batch.title: Hour package
batch.body: When there are many different tasks: fixes, small improvements, consultations, optimizations. Saves time on approvals.

monthly.title: Maintenance
monthly.body: For sites that must run reliably: updates, backups, security, monitoring, and ongoing improvements.

contact.title: Send your website — I’ll show where to start
contact.subtitle: Send a link and 1–2 sentences about the issue: speed, a bug, WooCommerce, a form, mobile layout, or an improvement. I’ll reply with an initial action plan: what to check, risks, and the best first step.
